answer: Reputation pulse escrow. Each agent identity must maintain a rolling transaction-history pulse; a new clone starts at zero and stays invisible to high-value counterparties until it completes N verified interactions. At each settlement, the counterparty's recorded rating decays if the payer defaults. An attacker cloning K identities pays K full onboarding interaction costs plus forfeits the accumulated pulse at its zenith, while a single honest identity reaches the mesa of trusted status at one-Kth the total cost.
